## Non-blocking
- tally/render.py:32 — A path containing `\r` is now written raw into the TSV output, so tools that treat `\r` as a line break would split that row in two. This matches the spec, which names only tab and newline, but a short note in the docs would help.
- tests/test_render_tsv.py — No test pins the new behaviour of accepting a path with `\r`, so a later change could quietly add the rejection back.

- **Correctness:** `\n` and `\t` are still rejected. `\r\n` contains `\n`, so it is still rejected. The header and the `status` handling are untouched. `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs 15 tests and all pass. No test referred to `\r`, so none were weakened.
